collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE VIII: OUR OWN STORIES, SKILLS AND FUTURE (LCH-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
From the owner's Volume IV concepts (301-400): telling our own stories, who owns a song or a design, research the village asks for, caregivers and builders, seeds that came home, makers and stargazers, terrible singing, newcomers who stay, and an island that belongs to its people.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: A weaver has a new pattern and the makers want their own festival: hold it, or show the work at the harvest feast.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) has woven a new pattern celebrating the year the village rebuilt after the storm. (friend), a potter, wants a festival just for makers, where everyone shows their work and swaps techniques. Others say it can wait for the harvest feast. What should they do?

text_only.reason: a celebration or a happy feeling in the story; no celebration happens in the game -- the draft's notes: everything but the marked effects is story only

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: The festival is a great success. Sculptors, potters, weavers and carvers show off and steal each other's tricks. (subject)'s pattern is the talk of the day. A child shows a very lumpy pot and is cheered just as loudly.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) hangs the new pattern at the harvest feast. People admire it between mouthfuls. It is nice. (friend) still thinks the makers deserve their own day, and starts planning it for next year.
